stem.en: The Vedas are called the earliest known body of Indian literature. Why can the writing of the Harappans not take that place?

text.en: The Harappan script has not yet been deciphered, so we cannot read it.
The Harappans did not use any form of writing.
All Harappan writing was destroyed when their cities were abandoned.
The Vedas were written down before the first Harappan cities were built.

explanation.en: The Harappans of the Sindhu-Sarasvatī civilisation had a script, but it has not yet been deciphered. The Vedas can be read, and they existed in oral form for several centuries before they were written down.
